console_output_chars_note: How many CHARACTERS of console output (Bash/PowerShell) a terminal may receive in one turn before the `own_reading` gate warns it (T42, 2026-09-24). 8000 = about 3600 tokens at 2.2 characters per token, the conversion MEASURED in T40 (calibrated table, source repo); T40 measured that the console is 21-33 % of what the orchestrator grows until its first lane, and with 8000, 13 of 186 turns and 21 of 340 warn (T42 measurement, source repo). Integer greater than 0; missing, 0, negative, decimal or text: 8000.
injected_handover_kb_note: How many KB of the handover are put in front of the terminal when it comes back from compacting (T18, 2026-09-22: from 12 to 16). Integer from 4 to 64; outside that, or no key, 16. Past the cap it is trimmed by sections and the last line says what is missing.
integration_branches_note: The branches NOBODY pushes to from a lane, not even with a git permit (gate `git_permit`, T5). If this key is missing, main, master and develop are used.
suites_note: Extractors of the `repeated_red` gate (T7, 2026-09-21). JSON allows no comments: the long explanation is in references/control-phase-1-and-2.md. Per entry: `name` (what the suite is called in the warnings), `command` (regex over the command that LAUNCHES it), `failure` (regex per line; group 1 is the IDENTIFIER of the failed test), `summary` (regex of the closing line with TWO groups: how many passed and how many failed; it is the best guarantee there is, because it lets the extracted failures be RECONCILED against what the suite says, and catches a truncated output or a run of zero tests), `end` (poorer alternative when the runner gives no numbers: it only says that the run FINISHED), `output_command` (regex of a command that SHOWS the output file; it is the only way the gate sees a suite launched in the background) and `active: false` to leave it declared and OFF. With no matching entry, the gate gives NO opinion.

suites.name: adversarial
suites._no_summary: Its closing line gives NO numbers (`ADVERSARIAL: no case broke the contract`), so this suite keeps the POOR guarantee: `end`. Declared consequence: if its output arrived truncated the gate detects it by the truncation, but it cannot RECONCILE extracted failures against reported failures as the other three do.
suites.end: ^ADVERSARIAL: (?:no case broke the contract|\d+ CASE\(S\) BREAK THE CONTRACT)\s*$

suites.name: generic-node-test
suites._why_off: It is the trap this gate exists NOT to repeat. A bare `/FAIL|Error/` matches `0 failed`, an `Error` inside a quoted log and even the comment that explains the problem, which is the same failure already paid for in `zero_unchecked`. It is written here so that whoever has a project with node --test / jest / vitest / pytest copies it, ADJUSTS it to their runner and turns it on with `active: true` knowingly. While `active` is false, the gate does not even look at it. The suite DOES turn it on in a temporary config to check that the anchored extractor tells real failures from the fixture's decoys.

conditional_angles.name: concurrency
conditional_angles.when: the diff touches parallel processes, locks, shared files, retries or global state
conditional_angles.question: what happens if two runs come in at the same time? is there a race between reading and writing?

conditional_angles.name: performance
conditional_angles.when: the diff adds loops over growing data, disk reads, or chained calls
conditional_angles.question: how much does this cost when the input is a hundred times larger?

conditional_angles.name: accessibility
conditional_angles.when: the diff touches an interface a person uses (markup, components, on-screen text)
conditional_angles.question: can it be used with a keyboard and a screen reader? is there an accessible name and contrast?

conditional_angles.name: i18n
conditional_angles.when: the diff touches visible text, dates, numbers, or string comparison and sorting
conditional_angles.question: does it break with accents, with another locale, or with much longer text?

conditional_angles.name: migrations
conditional_angles.when: the diff touches the data schema, the format of a state file, or the version of a ledger
conditional_angles.question: what happens to the data that ALREADY exists: integrity, compatibility and recovery? (reversibility, only if the contract asks for it)

conditional_angles.name: false positives and false negatives
conditional_angles.when: the diff adds or touches a check, a gate, a validator or a hook
conditional_angles.question: which legitimate input does it block too much, and which bad input does it let through?
